findings.title: Inverted comparison and wrong substring index in isAccessTokenId matcher
findings.body: In isAccessTokenId the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` is inverted: it rejects the token when the shortcut MATCHES the expected grant, so tests will fail on correct token IDs and pass on wrong ones. Additionally the index is wrong: the grant-type shortcut occupies characters 4-5 of the 6-char prefix, so it should be `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)` which grabs the last char of the token-type shortcut plus the first char of the grant shortcut. Every event assertion using this matcher (expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, expectAuthReqIdToToken) is broken.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check checks grantType instead of rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor contains `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` twice; the second occurrence should check `rawTokenId`. As a result a null rawTokenId is silently accepted and the "rawTokenId" error message is never produced for an actual null rawTokenId, weakening the intended precondition.

findings.title: Decoding malformed/unrecognized token IDs throws instead of degrading gracefully
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars, or when the session-type/token-type/grant shortcuts are unknown. This method is intended to be called on arbitrary incoming access tokens (e.g. tokens issued by another Keycloak version, a custom TokenContextEncoderProvider, or a custom grant with unregistered shortcut). A token with a colon but unexpected prefix format will cause an unhandled exception (500) in whatever endpoint later consumes this (introspection, userinfo, admin REST per the PR description). It should return UNKNOWN context rather than throwing, matching the no-colon fallback path.

findings.title: getShortcut() added to SPI interface without default method breaks third-party implementations
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is a public SPI (server-spi-private) that third-party grant-type providers implement. Adding the abstract method `String getShortcut()` without a default implementation makes every existing custom OAuth2GrantTypeFactory fail to compile/load at runtime after upgrade. A `default String getShortcut() { return getId(); }` (or similar) would preserve compatibility.

findings.title: Removal of public Context(Context) copy constructor is a source/behavioral break
findings.body: The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` was deleted and its behavior folded into the main constructor (which now reads grantType from formParams). Any external code subclassing or copying OAuth2GrantType.Context will no longer compile. Additionally, the grantType is now only captured at construction time from formParams; if setFormParams(...) is called afterwards (an existing public mutator), context.grantType becomes stale and will be encoded incorrectly into tokens issued via OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse.

findings.title: Lazy cache refresh can silently corrupt bidirectional grant shortcut maps with duplicates
findings.body: The duplicate-shortcut validation only runs once in postInit. getShortcutByGrantType/getGrantTypeByShortcut later mutate grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts for newly deployed providers without re-validating uniqueness: if a hot-deployed grant reuses an existing shortcut, grantsByShortcuts is overwritten so two grant types map to one shortcut while grantsToShortcuts keeps both, permanently desynchronizing encode/decode and producing tokens whose grant type decodes to the wrong grant.

findings.title: Unused import TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory
findings.body: The import org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.grants.TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory was added but the code uses the string constant OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE instead; the import is unused and should be removed.
